need: Tell which files a Python script inside a shell command writes, without counting paths that only appear in the text it writes.

searched.found: The ported code2check rule counts every path-like word in writing code; nothing reads the code's structure.

searched.where: Python standard library ast module; bashlex; Semgrep taint rules
searched.query: static analysis of file writes in python code
searched.found: ast parses the code exactly and is already installed; bashlex parses shell, not Python; Semgrep is a large dependency for one rule.

candidates.name: Python ast module
candidates.covers: Exact parse of the script, so calls and their arguments are known.
candidates.misses: Resolving a path built at run time; those keep the old rule.
candidates.reason: Standard library, a few dozen lines of call matching on top.

candidates.name: Semgrep
candidates.covers: Pattern and taint rules over Python.
candidates.misses: A heavy external binary in a hook that must answer in milliseconds.
candidates.reason: Too slow and large for an edit hook.
